newsitem.title: CHINA: China allows T-bills sales at higher prices.
newsitem.headline: China allows T-bills sales at higher prices.

text.p: Chinese underwriters have sold treasury bills to sub-underwriters at prices higher than face value for the first time since China revived state debt issues in the 1980s, the Shanghai Securities News said on Wednesday.

Wuhan Securities Co on Tuesday sold 1,074 lots of the nation's seven-year bonds at 102.5 yuan per bond against an issue price of 100 yuan on the Shanghai stock exchange, the newspaper said. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of T-bonds.
The seven-year bond, the first of its kind in China, is being issued from November 1 to November 20. It will be listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen bourses on November 21.
Beijing used to allow underwriters to sell treasury bonds only at their face value before listing, with the state compensating them for losses resulting from the issue cost.

This year the Finance Ministry, responsible for state debt issues, has taken many measures to reform the process. These include introducing public tenders to decide coupons before allowing underwriters to sell bonds at higher than issue prices.
